newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher, trailing Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher, trailing Chicago.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended higher across the board on Thursday, trailing the stronger Chicago market overnight, traders said.
Prices ranged from 120 yen to 170 yen per tonne higher.
Benchmark July 1998 closed 120 yen higher at 13,110 yen per tonne. Estimated volume was 47,487 lots.

"Short-covering emerged from the outset following the Chicago market," one trader said. "But further price gains may be limited. Although there is some concern over possible dry weather in the U.S., the overall crop conditions there have been good," one trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.49 per bushel at 0834 GMT, against $2.49-3/4 at Wednesday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean contract was traded at $7.85-1/4 per bushel at 0834 GMT, against $7.89 at Wednesday's close.
